codeReview.summary: The commit lands a substantial broker-backed project admin surface across auth-broker, web, and CLI, but the shipped CLI parity story is incomplete. I reproduced that a repo left on the default local ownership config still prints only local ownership after a broker-side shared registration, because the new CLI broker lookup is gated behind an already-shared local config. That means the browser registration flow described in the feature contract cannot be reliably compared with repo-bound CLI output, and shared/local conflicts can remain hidden.

issues.description: `resolveBrokerOwnershipView` returns early unless the local repo config already says `ownership.mode === "shared"`. In practice, registering a project through the new browser control-plane flow does not update `.hack/hack.config.json`, so a default-local repo still reports only local ownership in `hack project owner show --json` even when the broker has a shared registration for the same slug. I reproduced this with a repo-local CLI smoke using a default-local config plus a mocked broker response: the command emitted only `{ ownership: { mode: "local", ... } }` and no `broker_registration` or conflict payload.

The new CLI regression coverage only exercises repositories whose local config is already marked shared, so it never checks the default-local repo + broker-registration path that the feature's own manual verification step depends on. That missing negative check is why the CLI/local mismatch above shipped unnoticed.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Project visibility is now coupled directly to the existing org/team admin store: the auth-broker wires the project store from the same `orgTeamsStore`, and project access/owner resolution derives visibility from `listOrganizations` and `listTeams`. Regressions in org/team durability or membership scoping will now change which projects appear visible/owned.

The recorded worker verification does not satisfy the feature's own manual acceptance step. The contract required using agent-browser to register/administer a project and compare with repo-bound CLI ownership output, but the handoff only captured opening the unauthenticated shell, seeing the Projects nav link, and clicking `#projects`.

summary: Fail. Durable broker-side project registration/access work landed, but the repo-bound CLI does not reliably surface broker state from the default local-config path, so VAL-ADMIN-006's CLI/web parity claim is not fully met, and the captured manual verification evidence is weaker than the feature contract requires.
